explanation: The state of God in which believers experience complete rest from their own effort-based attempts at justification, serving as a picture of God's own Sabbath day after creation.
Trust and conviction that God keeps what He has promised, enabling people to enter His gift of grace without relying on their own works.
Divine speech or message from the Lord to humanity, often referring to Scripture, which is living and sharper than any sword because it discerns between soul and spirit.
The priestly service carried out by Jesus Christ in heaven, where He serves as eternal High Priest according to the order of Melchizedek to offer Himself once for all for the atonement of sins.
A serious exhortation not to let one's heart become hard or unwilling toward God's word as the Israelites did in the wilderness, which led them to lose the opportunity to enter His rest.
